title: US Unpredictability Is Giving Its Asian Allies New Reasons to Cooperate
author: Donggak Heo
text:
Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sane shakes hands with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the annual Australia–Japan Leaders’ Meeting, Canberra, Australia, May 4, 2026.
Credit: Prime Minister’s Office of Japan
When U.S. President Donald Trump abruptly ordered the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, officials in Seoul were caught off guard. The annual Ulchi Freedom Shield drills still went ahead, but were cut short on Trump’s order. The episode was a reminder that even one of Washington’s closest allies can find the assumptions of its security policy changed with little warning.That uncertainty is why, across the Indo-Pacific, several of the United States’ closest partners are investing more heavily in relationships with one another – and, increasingly, with Europe. South Korea and Japan are expanding cooperation on supply chains, energy and advanced industries. Japan and Australia are linking economic security more closely to defense production and military operations. All three are also building more structured ties with the European Union.[...]
